title: Krishna's Leelas with Kururamma
snippet: There are numerous stories about Krishna's leelas with Kururamma. Each one reveals the unusual intimacy He shared with His beloved devotee...
content:
There are numerous stories about Krishna's leelas with Kururamma. Each one reveals the unusual intimacy He shared with His beloved devotee.

Several legends describe how Vilwamangalam Swamiyar, who was believed to possess the divine vision to perceive the Lord's presence, recognised Krishna in the little boy who stayed with Kururamma.

One popular account narrates that Vilwamangalam Swamiyar once visited Kururamma's house to perform a special puja. During the worship, the flowers offered repeatedly fell at the feet of the little boy. This revealed His divine identity to the Swamiyar. However, Krishna gestured to him not to disclose His identity to Kururamma.

Krishna continued to play with Kururamma, happily accepting even her occasional punishments, just as any child would.

On one occasion, Kururamma, annoyed by His mischief, put Him inside a pot and covered it with another vessel, the one normally used for frying rice.

Meanwhile, Krishna was expected at Vilwamangalam Swamiyar's puja. When He failed to arrive on time, the Swamiyar became anxious.

Suddenly, Krishna appeared before him, running towards him with His entire body covered in charcoal powder.

When asked what had happened, Krishna innocently explained how Kururamma had confined Him inside the pot and how that had caused His delay.

Vilwamangalam Swamiyar was overwhelmed.

The very Bhagavan whose darshan even great sages considered a rare blessing had willingly allowed Himself to be confined inside a pot by His devotee!

He realised the extraordinary depth of Kururamma's devotion and regarded her with immense reverence.

There are many more such instances in the devotional traditions that reveal the intimate relationship between the devotee and the Divine.

### Her Final Journey

Kururamma's earthly journey eventually came to an end.

In 1640 AD, according to the devotional account, she prayed to Bhagavan to take her to His divine abode. Krishna graciously fulfilled her wish and took her to Sri Vaikuntha.

Kururamma disappeared without leaving behind her mortal remains.

Following her departure, her abandoned home gradually disintegrated. Yet the premises, believed to have been sanctified by the divine presence of Bhagavan Sri Krishna, remained under divine protection for nearly 360 years.

This sacred association eventually culminated in the consecration of the Kururamma Sree Krishna Temple at Vengilassery.

Thus, the story of a childless widow who found motherhood in the Divine became an enduring account of unconditional love and devotion.

### Krishna... The Divine in Every Form

Krishna... each devotee carries within their heart a form in which they wish to see Him.

For some, He is a little child to be loved and cared for. For others, He is a trusted friend, a brother, a beloved or a guiding force.

Whatever the relationship, everything begins with one's faith and belief.

The Divine presence surrounds us. It need not always reveal itself through extraordinary happenings or in the form we imagine. It may appear before anyone, in any form, at any moment in life.

Perhaps the Divine is not distant from us; it is our ability to recognise that presence that differs.

The realisation comes according to the depth of one's spiritual journey and the openness of one's heart.

Kururamma saw Krishna as her child, while others recognised Him as the Supreme Being. The Divine was the same; only the relationship through which He was experienced was different.

Perhaps that is the beauty of devotion.

We may see Krishna in the form we love, but the Divine remains one.

[CENTER]*Hare Krishna! Radhe Radhe!*
